svg.title: CPU datapath: instruction fetch, asynchronous register read, execution, and synchronous register write
svg.desc: HY-RV P1/F0/Q0 functional datapath. rv_frontend tracks one fetch owner and has no instruction response buffer. The SRAM adapter retains a stalled instruction response. insn_assemble and depth-zero rv_insn_link forward the token directly into the single backend IR. A sibling rv_branch_predictor selects static ANT or BTFNT; early JAL is disabled by default. Decode and execution functions are not separate occupied stages. Register read and write views belong to one physical 2R1W register file; I/D ports belong to one shared external SRAM. Clock wedges mark rising-edge state or enabled writes.
svg.text: Frontend + Q0 delivery overlap one execution IR. Functional regions do not imply independent pipeline stages.
One physical RAM · two logical I / D ports
Dashed links identify a shared resource; they are not data paths.

g.aria-label: rv_frontend request control. gen_pc_nxt is combinational; fetch_ctrl and fetch_tracker hold owner, held request and restart state. Displayed value is offered req_addr.
g.title: rv_frontend: combinational gen_pc_nxt selects held / redirect / boot / prediction; fetch_ctrl and fetch_tracker hold request/owner metadata.

g.aria-label: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, instruction port. One external shared RAM model. Request tracking and response outputs update on the positive edge. The marker describes the clocked port model; it does not claim the RAM array is made from flip-flops.
g.title: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, instruction port. One external shared RAM model. Request tracking and response outputs update on the positive edge. The marker describes the clocked port model; it does not claim the RAM array is made from flip-flops.

g.aria-label: rv_frontend insn_assemble plus sibling rv_insn_link at depth zero. Live instruction/fault token delivery is combinational; no instruction response buffer or queue register.
g.title: insn_assemble + rv_insn_link Q0: no response buffer. The memory producer holds response bits while the backend is busy. Local fault metadata has separate state.

g.aria-label: rv_core_simple.u_bp: rv_branch_predictor. Sibling static ANT or BTFNT policy, not a pipeline stage. Actual early JAL setting comes from the recorded build preset.
g.title: rv_branch_predictor: BP0 ANT default; BP1 BTFNT selectable. Backend checks actual successor; actual early JAL mode is recorded with the selected preset.
g.text: policy block, not a pipeline stage

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend : rv_backend. Inline positive-edge registers pc_pipe_r, insn_pipe_r, valid_pipe_r, and fetch-fault metadata. This is not a separate instantiated module.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend : rv_backend. Inline positive-edge registers pc_pipe_r, insn_pipe_r, valid_pipe_r, and fetch-fault metadata. This is not a separate instantiated module.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_decoder : rv32_decoder. Combinational decode, with additional encoding_legal filtering in rv_backend. No clocked decode stage.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_decoder : rv32_decoder. Combinational decode, with additional encoding_legal filtering in rv_backend. No clocked decode stage.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf, SYNC_READ=0, WB_FORWARD=0. Two asynchronous read ports of the same register file shown at the right. No read register.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf, SYNC_READ=0, WB_FORWARD=0. Two asynchronous read ports of the same register file shown at the right. No read register.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_alu : fu_alu, plus combinational operand selection and u_alu_op : rv32_alu_op_decode. The ALU has protocol clock pins but no edge-triggered datapath state in this configuration.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_alu : fu_alu, plus combinational operand selection and u_alu_op : rv32_alu_op_decode. The ALU has protocol clock pins but no edge-triggered datapath state in this configuration.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_br : fu_br. Combinational comparison, branch target, and jump-link result. Redirect and trap priority are selected in rv_backend.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_br : fu_br. Combinational comparison, branch target, and jump-link result. Redirect and trap priority are selected in rv_backend.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_mul : fu_mul, MUL_L=1. Combinational multiplication followed by positive-edge product, operation, valid, and tag state.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_mul : fu_mul, MUL_L=1. Combinational multiplication followed by positive-edge product, operation, valid, and tag state.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_div : fu_div. Positive-edge iterative state, accumulator, divisor, sign, operation, and counter registers. The backend also holds its instruction and wait counter.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_div : fu_div. Positive-edge iterative state, accumulator, divisor, sign, operation, and counter registers. The backend also holds its instruction and wait counter.

g.aria-label: Functional group in rv_backend, not a standalone LSU module: address from the shared u_alu; clocked execution substate and load_data_r plus combinational u_ls_split : rv32_ls_split and u_ls_align2 : rv32_ls_align2. The clock marker applies to response/control state, not to the byte-lane logic.
g.title: Functional group in rv_backend, not a standalone LSU module: address from the shared u_alu; clocked execution substate and load_data_r plus combinational u_ls_split : rv32_ls_split and u_ls_align2 : rv32_ls_align2. The clock marker applies to response/control state, not to the byte-lane logic.

g.aria-label: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, data port of the same RAM as the I port. Request tracking, responses, and enabled memory writes are positive-edge operations. This is not a second RAM instance or an all-flop SRAM claim.
g.title: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, data port of the same RAM as the I port. Request tracking, responses, and enabled memory writes are positive-edge operations. This is not a second RAM instance or an all-flop SRAM claim.

g.aria-label: Inline always_comb result mux in rv_backend. Selects the final result for the RF write port. No independent register, no extra pipeline stage, and no clock marker.
g.title: Inline always_comb result mux in rv_backend. Selects the final result for the RF write port. No independent register, no extra pipeline stage, and no clock marker.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf. One positive-edge write port, enabled only by wb_en and a nonzero destination. This is the same physical RF as the left read view.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_core.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf. One positive-edge write port, enabled only by wb_en and a nonzero destination. This is the same physical RF as the left read view.

svg.text: Register operands, immediates and PC feed the selected unit.
Clock wedge = positive-edge stored state or enabled write. RAM wedges mark the clocked interface/model, not an all-flop array.
Memory transfers occur on valid AND ready. Solid highlighted arrows mark accepted transfers; dashed amber arrows mark offered transfers waiting.
Highlights show logical activity in the selected trace sample, not physical switching. A register write occurs only when its recorded write enable is asserted.

g.title: Current PC and instruction-owner path
g.desc: Static RTL explanation, not measured internal state. gen_pc_nxt selects held offer, redirect, boot or prediction. fetch_tracker captures request PC and lookup metadata on acceptance. Memory holds instruction response until Q0/backend ready. The backend IR captures PC, instruction, fault and prediction metadata on admission. Old owner completion and replacement allocation can occur at one edge.
g.text: Current PC path · design explanation, not a measured internal waveform
gen_pc_nxt (combinational): held offer → pending redirect → boot → predicted successor → owner PC + 4
Memory response → assemble → Q0 → backend IR
If blocked, the SRAM adapter holds the response; no frontend buffer
IR admission + successor request may share one edge
Requires ready backend, response consumption, memory II=1
Ideal overlap: I retires + I+1 enters IR + I+2 fetch accepted. Redirect/fault/stall and multicycle execution can prevent it.
Fetch is driven by handshake/capacity, not directly by a commit pulse. Memory ownership and prediction metadata travel with the token.
